paper.title: Why do patients bypass primary care? Trust, resource concentration, and risk in China's tiered healthcare system: A comparative policy perspective.
paper.summary: China's tiered healthcare system seeks to direct patients to clinically appropriate levels of care, and yet many patients continue to seek care directly at higher-level hospitals. This Policy Forum proposes a conceptual explanation linking resource and capability concentration, perceived institutional trust differentials, risk-avoidant choice of providers, and the amplification of reputation through family and social networks. Illustrative comparisons with the United Kingdom, the United States, Japan, and South Korea reveal related but non-equivalent forms of alternative healthcare access under different arrangements. The framework does not treat bypassing a tier as inherently irrational or claim that the proposed pathways have been causally established. Instead, it suggests that credible primary care, reliable referral benefits, continuity of care, risk-sensitive rules on access, aligned financial incentives, and trustworthy quality information must be developed together. The proposed framework is intended to guide empirical testing and policy evaluation rather than to rank healthcare systems or estimate the prevalence with which care is bypassed.

paper.title: Acute Status Epilepticus Triggers Long-Term Neurogenic Niche Destabilization That Undermines Cognitive Function in the Excitotoxic FVB/N Hippocampus.
paper.summary: The adult hippocampus is highly susceptible to excitotoxic injury, although the extent to which acute seizure episodes dictate long-term cognitive outcomes through neurogenic niche remodeling remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the hypothesis that an isolated episode of sustained status epilepticus (SE) is sufficient to trigger persistent alteration of the adult neurogenic niche, followed by neurostructural and functional discrepancies. Acute SE was induced in young FVB/N mice via a single systemic dose of kainic acid. Dentate morphological remodeling was quantitatively characterized using immunostaining, Golgi-Cox staining, SNT-Sholl analysis, and confocal microscopy. Behavioral paradigms assessed anxiety, despair, and spatial/recognition memory, while correlation coefficient was used to establish structure-function correlations. Acute SE triggered the rapid activation of reactive adult neural stem cells (HopX+GFAP+), followed by a critical polarity shift and a fate transition from neurogenic (GFAP+S100β-) to non-neurogenic (GFAP+S100β+) lineages, thereby driving widespread reactive gliosis. This niche destabilization was accompanied by collapse of dentate neuronal architecture, characterized by ectopic DCX+ cell localization, asymmetrical neuronal clustering, primary dendritic ramification defects, abnormal and complex branching patterns, and disrupted dendritic spine microanatomy. These structural aberrations displayed a robust, graded correlation with increased anxiety, behavioral despair, and profound deficits in recognition and spatial memory. Our results demonstrate that even a discrete, acute seizure episode precipitates enduring disruption of the hippocampal adult neurogenic niche and long-lasting structural and behavioral abnormalities. This study highlights that early destabilization of the neurogenic niche is an underrecognized pathophysiological process associated with irreversible hippocampal remodeling and cognitive deficits following SE.

paper.title: Approaches in Opioid Pharmacology: Toward Safer Pain Management.
paper.summary: Opioids are crucial for pain management, but the traditional mu-opioid receptor agonists are associated with considerable risk, such as addiction, overdose, and serious side effects such as respiratory depression. This review aims to emphasize the recent developments in the development of safer opioids, including approaches such as mixed agonists at MOR, KOR, and DOR, biased agonists at MOR, KOR, and DOR, and allosteric modulation. Other approaches, such as peripherally acting opioids and agonists at MOR splice variants, are also discussed as safer options for pain management without the risk of central side effects.

paper.title: A novel anti-depression strategy utilizing γ-CD-MOFs delivery system for volatile oil from Alpiniae Oxyphyllae fructus - examining the mechanism of gut microbiota and neuroinflammation.
paper.summary: The volatile oil extracted from Alpiniae Oxyphyllae Fructus (AOVO) exhibits excellent anti-inflammatory properties but is unstable. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a cyclodextrin-based drug delivery system employing γ-cyclodextrin metal-organic frameworks (γ-CD-MOFs) to encapsulate AOVO, and examine its potential antidepressant mechanisms by integrating multi-omics approaches. The AOVO/γ-CD-MOFs system exhibited a well-ordered crystalline structure. Physicochemical analyses confirmed the successful encapsulation of AOVO within the γ-CD-MOFs matrix. This encapsulation enhanced the stability, solubility, and cumulative release rate of AOVO, augmenting its biosafety, and antidepressant effects of AOVO in vivo. Based on the predicted antidepressant mechanisms of the identified components of AOVO in vivo, the current study confirmed that the formulation improved the integrity of the intestinal barrier and reduced the level of pro-inflammatory cytokines, which were positively associated with the increased abundance of Ligilactobacillus. This shift helped in antagonizing the cascade of responses associated with neuroinflammation triggered by the peripheral inflammatory stimulation. Meanwhile, AOVO/γ-CD-MOFs prolonged fluorescence signals in brain and alleviated neuroinflammation, thereby exerting an antidepressant effect. Overall, this study developed a promising food-grade strategy for encapsulating and stabilizing volatile oil therapeutic agents, and proposed a new scheme for treating depression using the fabricated AOVO/γ-CD-MOFs system. These findings provide a preclinical proof-of-concept for using food-grade γ-CD-MOFs to stabilize volatile oil therapeutic agents and improve their delivery performance.

paper.title: Dealcoholized muscadine wine improved skin elasticity and oxidative stress biomarkers without affecting gut microbiome in women over 40 in a randomized controlled trial.
paper.summary: Muscadine wine has a unique polyphenol profile distinct from that of common wine, and limited research exists on its health benefits. This study aimed to investigate the effects of intake of dealcoholized muscadine wine (DMW) on skin health, oxidative stress, inflammatory biomarkers, and the gut microbiome. Seventeen healthy women were randomly assigned to consume 300 mL of DMW or a placebo daily for 6 weeks, separated by a 3-week washout period, in a randomized, single-blinded, crossover design. Skin health parameters were measured on the face and forearm. Oxidative stress and inflammatory biomarkers were assessed in plasma. Fecal bacterial DNA was sequenced using shotgun sequencing. DMW did not affect UVB-induced erythema compared to placebo. However, it significantly decreased transepidermal water loss and increased facial gross elasticity. Skin elasticity significantly improved on the forearm, whereas other skin parameters were not affected. DMW significantly decreased plasma levels of matrix metalloproteinase-9 and advanced glycation end products compared with placebo. However, the abundance, diversity, and functions of the gut microbiome were not affected. Polyphenol-rich DMW administered for six weeks improved certain skin health parameters and reduced oxidative and inflammatory stress, without affecting the gut microbiome in healthy women.

paper.title: Advances in cereal protein applications for infant and Young child nutrition.
paper.summary:
BACKGROUND: The increasing use of plant-derived proteins in infant and young child nutrition necessitates tailored amino acid profiles, high digestibility and strict safety controls. Cereal proteins, such as rice, oat, maize, millet, barley, and wheat, are widely used in complementary foods but face intrinsic limitations, notably lysine and tryptophan deficits, antinutritional factors that reduce bioavailability, gluten immunogenicity in wheat/barley, and inorganic arsenic risks in rice.
SCOPE AND APPROACH: This review synthesizes recent advances in processing and formulation strategies, including enzymatic hydrolysis, fermentation, germination, extrusion, cereal-legume complementation, and micronutrient fortification. Their impacts on digestibility, techno-functionality, iron and zinc bioavailability, and protein quality, including Protein Digestibility-Corrected Amino Acid Score (PDCAAS) and Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score (DIAAS) are critically reviewed using data from in vitro assays, product development, and clinical trials.
KEY FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS: Processing and blending approaches can substantially improve protein digestibility, amino acid balance and micronutrient availability, and hydrolyzed rice protein holds clinical promise for cow's milk protein allergy (CMPA). However, most evidence is preclinical, reporting of protein quality is inconsistent, and industrial translation is constrained by sensory, shelf-life, contaminant and cost issues. We recommend standardized DIAAS-based reporting, large-scale feeding trials, sensory /stability optimization, and targeted exploration of underutilized grains (e.g., oat, millet) with active allergen monitoring. Prioritizing amino acid-focused formulation coupled with strategies to enhance micronutrient bioavailability will accelerate safe adoption of cereal proteins in early-life nutrition.

paper.title: Pseudo-latex coatings formed by zein-based nanoparticle aqueous dispersions: Promising packaging for sustainable, effective, and multifunctional preservation of fruits and vegetables.
paper.summary: Postharvest losses of fruits and vegetables pose a global challenge to food systems, highlighting the urgent need to develop green and efficient preservation technologies, such as protective coatings. Zein, a renewable and biodegradable plant protein, exhibits remarkable film-forming and barrier properties. However, conventional zein-based coatings derived from high-concentration ethanol-water mixtures with zein dissolved in (Zsol) face notable limitations, including safety concerns, poor qualities, as well as difficulties in employment and multifunctional integration. To address these shortcomings, recent research has shifted toward the development of zein-based nanoparticle aqueous dispersions (Zdis) as coating matrix. Firstly, preparation approaches were elaborated, with emphasis on antisolvent precipitation (ASP) and pH-driven method (PDM), discussing underlying principles, advantages, and current challenges. Subsequently, stabilization principles of Zdis at the colloidal level under quantitative framework were critically examined. From the perspective of functional design, plasticizer selection, loading of bioactive compounds (BCs), and adhesion enhancement were explored to synergistically optimize comprehensive performance. Therefore, the compatibility (preservation effects, failure mechanisms, and sensory impact) of Zdis-based coatings on diverse fruits and vegetables were elucidated. The importance of coating approaches, drying means, intelligent supervision for integrated processes, sustainability assessment concepts, and safety regulations was also emphasized. Finally, key challenges for scale-up integration and future perspective were proposed. Overall, Zdis offers a promising platform and basis for advancing postharvest preservation toward sustainability and high efficacy.

paper.title: Structure-dependent modulation of Morchella esculenta protein by ferulic and chlorogenic acids: Improving techno-functionality and digestibility of a fungal alternative protein.
paper.summary: Fungal proteins face poor processing functionality and low digestibility limiting their use in emulsified and structured foods. Here, Morchella esculenta protein (MP) was modified by ferulic acid (FA) and chlorogenic acid (CA) at 0.0375-1 mg/mL. Both phenolics bound MP concentration-dependently, CA exhibited stronger binding affinity (Ka = 3.242 × 106 L/Mol) and deeper conformational rearrangement, while FA relied on hydrophobic and π-π interactions. Moderate phenolic addition maximized MP performance: EAI rose from 2.44 to 3.99 m2/g and digestibility from 45.33% to 58.31%, with CA delivering superior antioxidant capacity (DPPH scavenging 69.67%). Excess phenolics triggered severe protein aggregation and weakened interfacial stability. This work clarifies structure-dependent differential regulation of MP by two phenolics, defines optimal concentration thresholds, and provides theoretical support for clean-label fungal protein food ingredients.

paper.title: Fermented red quinoa alleviates sleep deprivation-induced anxiety-like behavior and inflammation associated with gut microbiota modulation.
paper.summary: Chronic sleep deprivation (SD) induces systemic inflammation and significantly increases the risk of neuropsychiatric disorders, including anxiety. Our previous findings demonstrated that Lactobacillus kisonensis (L. kisonensis)-fermented red quinoa (RQF) was enriched with polyphenols possessing anti-inflammatory potential. However, whether RQF confers neuroprotection against SD-induced injury remains unexplored. This study therefore examined this effect and underlying mechanisms in a murine model of chronic SD. C57BL/6 J mice were subjected to SD (20 h/d for 4 weeks) using an SD apparatus and simultaneously administered RQF supernatant daily via oral gavage (20 mL/kg·body weight, containing 5 × 108 CFU/mL L. kisonensis). Our results showed that RQF treatment elevated central entries, visit time, and distance in the open field test, as well as time spent in open arms in the elevated plus maze test, suggesting reduced anxiety-like behavior. RQF also preserved hippocampal synaptic ultrastructure, as observed by transmission electron microscopy. Mechanistically, RQF partially modulated the mRNA expression of circadian rhythm genes (Bmal1, Clock, Per, Cry) in the liver, brain, and colon, while upregulating antioxidant enzyme genes (Cat, Gpx, Sod) and suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (Tnf-α, Il-6, Il-1β). Moreover, RQF upregulated tight junction proteins (ZO-1, Ocln, Cldn1) and reduced serum LPS levels, collectively indicating improved intestinal barrier integrity. Furthermore, RQF increased gut microbiota diversity, reduced the relative abundance of the pro-inflammatory genus Faecalibaculum, and enriched short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)-producing genera, including Muribaculum and Duncaniella. Targeted SCFA analysis confirmed that RQF significantly elevated fecal isobutyric, isovaleric, and caproic acids, and upregulated the mRNA expression of SCFA receptors (Ffar2, Ffar3), the downstream target Npy, and Hdac3. In conclusion, RQF supplementation alleviates SD-induced anxiety-like behavior and inflammation, an effect associated with gut-brain axis modulation. These findings suggest that fermented red quinoa may represent a promising dietary strategy against sleep deprivation-induced neurobehavioral deficits.

paper.title: Modulating stress responses via the microbiota-gut-brain axis: a pathway-focused review of GABA, 5-HT, and kynurenine metabolites.
paper.summary: Stress is a major risk factor for human anxiety, depression, and other neuropsychiatric disorders, yet nutritional strategies that target upstream biological mechanisms remain insufficiently developed. Growing evidence indicates that host-microbiota co-regulated metabolites act as functional mediators within the microbiota-gut-brain axis, shaping individual vulnerability or resilience to stress. In this review, we synthesize current preclinical and human evidence with a focus on three metabolite systems of high mechanistic relevance-γ-aminobutyric acid, serotonin, and kynurenine-pathway metabolites. We discuss how microbial activity, host metabolism, and dietary inputs interact to modulate brain-relevant signaling under stress. We highlight neuroendocrine, neuroimmune, and neural pathways through which these systems may act, including stress-induced disruptions in intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity and amplification of inflammatory signaling. Evidence across models suggests that stress-associated dysbiosis alters GABAergic and serotonergic signaling and shifts tryptophan metabolism toward neuroactive kynurenines, thereby biasing neural excitability, synaptic plasticity, and affect-related behaviors. We further evaluate food-based psychobiotic strategies-such as targeted whole-food matrices, fermented foods, and selected probiotic strains-that can reprogram microbial metabolism to restore neurotransmitter balance and attenuate inflammation. Finally, we propose a translational framework emphasizing strain- and pathway-specific mechanisms, standardized metabolite quantification, and biomarker-guided personalization to advance microbiome-metabolite interventions for stress-related brain dysfunction.

paper.title: The role of peptides in regulating dough quality: A comprehensive review.
paper.summary: Dough-based foods (DBFs) face persistent challenges, including nutritional limitations and quality deterioration. Peptides have shown great potential in improving dough quality. However, the wide variety of peptides leads to diverse effects on DBFs. The review summarizes the effects of source and employed protease of peptides on dough quality improvement efficacy, discussing key factors from a structural and functional perspective. It then analyzes the regulatory mechanisms by focusing on peptides interactions with key dough components: gluten, starch and fermentative microorganisms. Through a critical analysis of peptides' properties and their interactions with the dough matrix, the work aims to clarify the multi-target pathways of peptides regulating dough quality. Based on structure-function relationships, three core functional categories of peptide-based dough improvers are proposed, with corresponding preliminary design principles. Current applications of peptides in baked, boiled, and steamed DBFs are summarized, and critical challenges limiting their industrialization are identified. Finally, the review proposes structured future research directions to guide the targeted development of peptide-based dough improvers.
